fullPassage: Conventional wisdom holds that in order to make progress, it is necessary to set goals. But it may be more helpful to reframe objectives as continuous systems. According to Professor Adam Alter, when we set goals, we position ourselves in a perpetual state of failure. What he means by this is that until the specific goal is achieved, we have not met our target and therefore view ourselves as not yet being successful. Once we do meet our target, however, the satisfaction we derive from our success is ultimately short-lived because we are inclined to immediately set a new goal, placing ourselves once again in the familiar territory of failure. Alter suggests that instead of taking this approach, which focuses on the end result, we should engage in consistent activities that lead to the target but that allow for a sense of progress and achievement on a daily basis. For instance, rather than setting the goal of writing 100,000 words in six months, one might establish a system of writing 500 words each morning for an hour. By following this method, one not only works toward the larger objective but also experiences regular success.

④ create(만들다) ✅ 정답 — establish와 동의어
det.tip: establish(세우다) = create(만들다)

questions.passage: Conventional wisdom holds that in order to make progress, it is necessary to set goals. But it may be more helpful to reframe objectives as <u>continuous</u> systems. According to Professor Adam Alter, when we set goals, we position ourselves in a perpetual state of failure. What he means by this is that until the specific goal is achieved, we have not met our target and therefore view ourselves as not yet being successful. Once we do meet our target, however, the satisfaction we derive from our success is ultimately short-lived because we are inclined to immediately set a new goal, placing ourselves once again in the familiar territory of failure. Alter suggests that instead of taking this approach, which focuses on the end result, we should engage in consistent activities that lead to the target but that allow for a sense of progress and achievement on a daily basis. For instance, rather than setting the goal of writing 100,000 words in six months, one might establish a system of writing 500 words each morning for an hour. By following this method, one not only works toward the larger objective but also experiences regular success.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 continuous와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
continuous는 '끊이지 않고 계속되는'이라는 뜻으로, 정반대는 '간헐적인, 이따금 끊기는'을 뜻하는 intermittent
① intermittent(간헐적인) ✅ 정답 — continuous의 반의어
② endless(끝없는) — 오히려 동의어에 가까운 함정
③ smooth(매끄러운) — 의미축이 다른 단어
④ ongoing(계속 진행 중인) — 동의어에 가까운 함정
det.tip: continuous(지속적인) ↔ intermittent(간헐적인). endless·ongoing은 오히려 비슷한 뜻이므로 함정

questions.passage:
(A) Even after months of hard work, the team had not met their <u>target</u>, so they felt they had failed to succeed.
(B) The archer drew her bow, aimed carefully, and struck the <u>target</u> right in the center with her final arrow.
questions.stem: 다음 밑줄 친 target이 (A)의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
(A)의 target은 이루고자 하는 '목표'라는 추상적 의미로 쓰였음
① enemy target(적 표적) ❌ (B)처럼 물리적으로 겨냥하는 대상
② hit the target with her arrows(과녁) ❌ 화살로 맞히는 구체적 과녁
③ annual sales target(연간 판매 목표) ✅ 정답 — 이루려는 '목표'라는 추상적 의미로 (A)와 동일
④ stared at the target(표적) ❌ 훈련에서 바라보는 구체적 대상
det.tip: target은 추상적으로 '목표', 구체적으로 '과녁·표적'을 의미함

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "continuing for a very long time without stopping or changing"

det.analysis:

① temporary(일시적인) — 잠깐 지속되는 것으로 정의와 반대
② occasional(가끔의) — 이따금 일어나는 것으로 정의와 다름
③ sudden(갑작스러운) — 지속성이 아니라 발생 방식과 관련
④ perpetual(영속적인) ✅ 정답 — 정의와 정확히 일치
det.tip: perpetual = 멈추지 않고 아주 오래 계속되는

questions.passage: According to Professor Adam Alter, when we set goals, we position ourselves in a perpetual state of failure. What he means by this is that until the specific goal is __________ (achieve), we have not met our target and therefore view ourselves as not yet being successful.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 빈칸 앞에 be동사(is)가 있고, 목표가 '달성되는' 대상이므로 수동태 형태인 achieved로 써야 함
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞 is와 함께 수동태를 이루어야 하므로 achieve의 과거분사형 achieved가 정답
주어 the specific goal(구체적 목표)은 '달성되는' 대상이므로 능동(achieve)이 아닌 수동(be + p.p.) 형태가 필요함
det.tip: be동사 + 과거분사(p.p.) = 수동태. achieve → achieved

questions.passage: For instance, rather than setting the goal of writing 100,000 words in six months, one might establish a system of writing 500 words each morning for an hour. By following this method, one not only works toward the larger objective but also __________ (experience) regular success.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 주어 one은 3인칭 단수이고, 앞의 동사 works와 병렬을 이루므로 experience에 -s를 붙여 experiences로 써야 함
det.analysis:
'not only A but also B' 구조에서 빈칸은 앞의 동사 works와 병렬을 이루는 자리이며, 주어 one이 3인칭 단수이므로 동사에 -s를 붙인 experiences가 정답
does/do 없이 현재시제 단수 주어이므로 원형 experience를 그대로 쓰면 수 일치에 어긋남
det.tip: 주어 one(3인칭 단수) + not only works but also ___ → 병렬·수 일치로 experiences

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
